rv.q: In Ren, Dillman has written a complex character who makes decisions that are often understandable yet morally fraught.
But as an exploration of women aging into invisibility, it misses the mark.
NO SUCH THING is a drama about people, real people.
It’s a purposeful and powerful treatise that asks its audience to consider such realities as they arise in life, as well as one person’s way in dealing with them.
Dillman's No Such Thing is ultimately a refreshing and welcome portrait.
With its total focus on the private and the domestic, “No Such Thing” never pulls us in.
Stampley has created something special on this very small intimate stage.

cn.t: Dillman's world premiere about an older woman's affair and family secrets earns mostly positive reviews for its provocative premise, though some critics find the dual plotlines underdeveloped and the focus on wealthy characters limiting.
